summary: The toast() page documents every way to render a Sonner toast and lists the per-toast options with their defaults. A plain string becomes the title, and an options object passed as the second argument overrides any options set on <Toaster />. The typed variants add meaning: success shows a checkmark icon, error shows an error icon, action and cancel render primary and secondary buttons that close the toast, promise toasts move from loading to a result automatically, loading toasts show a spinner, and custom and headless toasts let you supply your own JSX. The API reference lists the per-toast defaults, including duration 4000, position bottom-right, dismissible true, closeButton false and containerAriaLabel 'Notifications'. For a design system this is the catalogue of toast variants and the baseline values to lock. [inferred]
key_ideas: Calling toast() with just a string makes that string the title.
Options passed to toast() override the options set on <Toaster />.
Success toasts show a checkmark icon in front of the message, and error toasts show an error icon.
An action is a primary button: clicking it runs onClick and closes the toast, unless onClick calls event.preventDefault().
A cancel is a secondary button that also runs onClick and closes the toast.
Both action and cancel can be JSX, such as your own <Button>.
A promise toast starts in a loading state and updates itself when the promise resolves or fails; its messages can be functions of the result or error.
A loading toast shows a spinner and is for when you handle the states yourself instead of using a promise toast.
Custom toasts take JSX as the first argument and keep the default styling.
Headless toasts are unstyled custom JSX that keep the functionality and receive the Toast as an argument.
Default per-toast values: duration 4000, position bottom-right, dismissible true, closeButton false, invert false, containerAriaLabel Notifications.

rules.why: A string passed on its own becomes the title.

rules.rule: Use the error toast for failures so an error icon appears in front of the message.
rules.why: Error renders an error icon in front of the message.

rules.rule: Use the action option to put a primary button in the toast; clicking it closes the toast and runs the callback passed via onClick.
rules.why: Action renders a primary button, and clicking it closes the toast and runs the callback passed via onClick.
rules.evidence: Renders a primary button, clicking it will close the toast and run the callback passed via onClick

rules.rule: Call event.preventDefault() inside the action's onClick when the toast must stay open after the action is clicked.
rules.why: By default clicking the action closes the toast; preventDefault stops that.
rules.evidence: You can prevent the toast from closing by calling event.preventDefault()

rules.rule: Pass your own JSX, such as a <Button> component, as the action when the default action button is not enough.
rules.why: The docs show that you can render JSX as your action.
rules.evidence: You can also render jsx as your action.

rules.rule: Use the cancel option to put a secondary button in the toast; clicking it closes the toast and runs the callback passed via onClick.
rules.why: Cancel renders a secondary button, and clicking it closes the toast and runs the callback passed via onClick.
rules.evidence: Renders a secondary button, clicking it will close the toast and run the callback passed via onClick

rules.rule: Pass your own JSX as the cancel when the default cancel button is not enough.
rules.why: The docs show that you can render JSX in the cancel option.
rules.evidence: You can also render jsx in the cancel option.

rules.rule: Use a promise toast for async work, so the toast starts loading and switches to success or error on its own when the promise settles.
rules.why: A promise toast starts in a loading state and updates automatically after the promise resolves or fails.
rules.evidence: Starts in a loading state and will update automatically after the promise resolves or fails.

rules.rule: Pass functions as a promise toast's success and error messages so the message includes the promise's result or error.
rules.why: The docs say you can pass a function to the success/error messages to incorporate the result or error.
rules.evidence: You can pass a function to the success/error messages

rules.rule: Return an object of toast options from a promise toast's success or error function when the result toast needs more detail.
rules.why: The docs say you can return an object with toast options if you need more detailed toasts.
rules.evidence: If you need more detailed toasts, you can return an object with toast options.

rules.rule: Use a loading toast (spinner) only when you handle the loading, success and error states yourself; otherwise use a promise toast.
rules.why: The loading toast is useful when you want to handle various states yourself instead of using a promise toast.
rules.evidence: Useful when you want to handle various states yourself instead of using a promise toast.

rules.why: This renders a custom toast while keeping the default styling.
rules.evidence: You can pass jsx as the first argument instead of a string to render a custom toast while maintaining default styling.

rules.rule: For a fully custom look, use the headless toast: render your own unstyled JSX, which keeps the functionality and receives the Toast as an argument.
rules.why: Headless renders an unstyled toast with custom JSX while keeping the functionality and giving access to all toast properties.
rules.evidence: Use it to render an unstyled toast with custom jsx while maintaining the functionality.

process.detail: Choose plain, success, error, action, cancel, promise, loading, custom or headless based on what the message needs.
Add an options object as the second argument (description, icon, action, cancel, duration, position and so on); these override the <Toaster /> options.

For a promise, use the promise toast: it shows loading, then success or error. Pass functions for the success and error messages to include the result or error, and return an object of toast options for more detail.
Give action and cancel an onClick. Both close the toast after running; call event.preventDefault() in the action's onClick to keep it open.
